_info.comment: An INTERACTION: EIP-161's definition of an empty account changes WHICH CONDITION governs SELFDESTRUCT's account-creation charge, not merely its size. Before EIP-161 the 25,000 is charged when the beneficiary DOES NOT EXIST, and the dying contract's balance is irrelevant. From EIP-161 it is charged only when the beneficiary is EMPTY *and* the dying contract holds a balance. The two conditions agree on a funded contract and disagree on an empty one, which is the whole of this file.
_info.eips: EIP-161 at Atlantis, interacting with SELFDESTRUCT's gas as repriced by EIP-150 at Gas Reprice and by EIP-2929 at Magneto.

theTwoReadings.0x10: A helper holding NOTHING destroys itself to a beneficiary that does not exist. This is the discriminating case: 30,728 through Defuse, then 5,728 from Atlantis, because the 25,000 stops being charged.
theTwoReadings.0x11: A helper holding one ether does the same. This is the control: it pays the 25,000 at every label from Gas Reprice on, because both conditions are satisfied under either rule.

_info.whyTheCONTROLIsTheLoadBearingHalf: Slot 0x10 alone is a number that changes at Atlantis, which a dozen unrelated rules could also produce. Read beside 0x11 it is specific: the two differ by exactly 25,000 from Atlantis and by exactly nothing before it. A client that dropped the charge entirely moves both; a client that kept the pre-EIP-161 condition moves neither.
_info.whatNoOtherFixtureHere Sees: selfdestruct_refund.json uses a funded helper only, so it exercises the case where the two conditions agree and can never see the divergence. This file exists for the empty-helper case and nothing else in the suite reaches it.
_info.theFullShapeOfTheBoundaries: Frontier and Homestead read 68 because SELFDESTRUCT is free before EIP-150. Gas Reprice through Defuse read 30,728. Atlantis and Phoenix read 5,728. Magneto and Spiral read 10,228, the extra 4,500 being EIP-2929's cold-account access on the beneficiary. Four boundaries in one column.
_info.oracle: core-geth's own statetest runner, which is not the implementation under certification.
_info.oracle-version: core-geth modernized 1.13.0-26975d6a. Production v1.12.21 cannot be used: its t8n fork table has no ETC_DieHard, ETC_Gotham or ETC_DefuseDifficultyBomb.
_info.signing: txbytes carries the signed transaction. Legacy signature through Gas Reprice, replay-protected from Die Hard.
_info.unfilled-no-fork-name: No expectation for ETC_Thanos: the generator's fork table has no name for it.
_info.unfilled-not-a-state-rule: No expectation for ETC_DAOFork, ETC_DAOWars, ETC_FrontierThawing, ETC_MESSOff, ETC_MESSOn.

wrongBuildScores.method: Scored 2026-08-25 against real broken builds of the reference client, patched at both code paths -- gas_table.go governs the labels before Magneto and operations_acl.go from Magneto on.
wrongBuildScores.eip161ConditionWithoutTheBalanceTest: 9/12, and THIS is the defect that justifies the file. A client that tests the beneficiary's emptiness but not the dying contract's balance charges the 25,000 on an empty helper where it should not. selfdestruct_refund.json does NOT catch it -- its helper is funded, so the correct and the broken condition agree there. Confirmed on both paths.
wrongBuildScores.keepsThePreEip161Condition: 9/12 here, and also caught by selfdestruct_refund at 9/12 -- so this file is not what makes that defect visible.
wrongBuildScores.creationChargeDroppedEntirely: 9/12 here, also caught by selfdestruct_refund at 9/12.
wrongBuildScores.whatTheThreeTogetherShow: Two of the three defects are caught by the older fixture as well; one is not. That one is the whole marginal value of this file and it was measured rather than assumed -- the file was built first, found to catch nothing the older one missed, and kept only once a defect it uniquely catches had been constructed and run.
